chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who has sheep, from which he milks a large quantity of milk every day. What do you say about the one who buys five hundred ratls (a unit of weight) from him, or more than that, one hundred ratls for a specific amount of dirhams, and then takes from him a certain number of ratls every day until he fulfills what he bought from him? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with this and similar cases.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy milk in advance by weight and receive it gradually?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the validity of 'bay' al-safah' (sale of deferred delivery) for perishable goods like milk, where a fixed weight is purchased but delivered incrementally over time. It highlights the Shia juristic acceptance of this specific commercial structure, distinguishing it from riba (usury) by ensuring the commodity exists and is measurable, thereby facilitating trade in agricultural products without requiring immediate full possession.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al Hannat who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happened to have sheep for him which used to give him a lot of milk during every day. What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the one who buys five hundred ratls (units of measurement) from him, or more than that one hundred ratls with such and such Dirhams, so he would take from him certains ratls during every day until he fulfils what he bought from him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with this and approximate to it’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Wallad al-Hannat who has said the following: “

This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man saying, ‘He has sheep that milks and the milk is abundant every day, if one can buy from him five hundred Ritl (a certain unit of measurement) or more and every one hundred Ritl for so and so much dirham then every day take certain Ritl until the deal is complete.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful (for this) and similar things.’”
